rows.title: GPT Actions Privacy & Policy Audit
rows.summary: Audit 2,253 real GPT Actions against OpenAI's published GPT Actions Usage Policy and compute cross-domain data-exposure amplification across shared backend domains on a Linux VM.
rows.task_prompt:
You are working on a Linux VM to perform a compliance audit of GPT Actions against OpenAI's published GPT Actions Usage Policy. All inputs are staged locally on this VM. No network access is required or permitted.

## Input Files (read-only)
- Pre-classified Action data: `base/input/pp_action_data_entities.json`
- Data taxonomy (CSV, UTF-8 BOM): `base/input/taxonomy.csv`
- OpenAI GPT Actions Usage Policy + Policy-to-Taxonomy Mapping Guide: `base/input/openai_gpt_actions_usage_policy.md`
- GPT → Action metadata: `base/input/gpt_action_metadata.json`

## Your Task
1. Parse all four input files using only Python 3 standard library modules (`json`, `csv`, `re`, `collections`).
   - If you want to script the audit, use the canonical task-local Python entry point `base/software/python`. It `exec`s the preinstalled system interpreter at `/usr/bin/python`.
2. Apply the Policy-to-Taxonomy Mapping Guide inside the policy markdown verbatim — it is the authoritative mapping from taxonomy `data_type` values to CRITICAL and HIGH violations.
3. Produce `output/policy_violations.json` as a JSON document with `total_violations`, `severity_breakdown` (CRITICAL/HIGH counts), and `violations`: a list with one entry per offending Action field. Each entry must include `severity`, `policy_clause`, `action_domain`, `api_name`, `data_field_name`, and `data_type`. Entries missing `policy_clause` or `action_domain` will be discarded before scoring.
4. Produce `output/cross_domain_exposure_report.csv` with the header `domain,gpt_count,action_count,avg_datatypes_per_action,union_datatypes_count,amplification_factor,union_datatypes`. Include exactly one row for every backend `domain` served by at least 3 distinct GPTs. `amplification_factor` is `f"{round(union_datatypes_count / avg_datatypes_per_action, 3)}x"` (three-decimal numeric prefix plus trailing `x`). `union_datatypes` is a semicolon-delimited, alphabetically sorted list of the distinct `data_type` values.

## Hints
- `taxonomy.csv` begins with a UTF-8 BOM — open it with `encoding="utf-8-sig"`.
- Keys in `pp_action_data_entities.json` are literal `"<domain>, <api_name>"` strings separated by `", "` (comma + single space). Split on the first `", "` only; some `api_name` values contain commas.
- Do not modify any file under `input/`.
- Write only to `output/`.
agent_must_do: Parse `pp_action_data_entities.json`, `taxonomy.csv`, `openai_gpt_actions_usage_policy.md`, and `gpt_action_metadata.json` with only Python stdlib modules.
Apply the Policy-to-Taxonomy Mapping Guide verbatim to flag CRITICAL and HIGH taxonomy types per Action field.

Write `output/policy_violations.json` with `total_violations`, `severity_breakdown`, and per-field violation records carrying `severity`, `policy_clause`, `action_domain`, `api_name`, `data_field_name`, and `data_type`.

Write `output/cross_domain_exposure_report.csv` with one row per backend domain served by ≥ 3 distinct GPTs, computing amplification as `round(union_datatypes_count / avg_datatypes_per_action, 3)` suffixed with `x`.

input_files.name: pp_action_data_entities.json
input_files.description: Pre-classified data collection profiles for 2,253 GPT Actions, keyed by `"<backend_domain>, <api_name>"`. Each Action lists its data fields with an assigned taxonomy `data_type`.

input_files.name: taxonomy.csv
input_files.description: Data taxonomy reference (category, data type, description) used to interpret each field's `data_type`.

input_files.name: openai_gpt_actions_usage_policy.md
input_files.description: OpenAI's published GPT Actions Usage Policy with a Policy-to-Taxonomy Mapping Guide that enumerates CRITICAL and HIGH taxonomy types.

input_files.name: gpt_action_metadata.json
input_files.description: Mapping of 3,116 GPT IDs to their embedded Actions and backend domains, used to compute GPT counts per backend domain.

rows.title: SSE Northbound Programmatic Trading Research
rows.summary: Answer three closed-book Shanghai Stock Exchange reporting questions from staged Chinese source documents and return a structured JSON memo with Chinese citations and evidence.
rows.task_prompt:
You are acting as a regulatory consultant on Shanghai Stock Exchange Northbound programmatic-trading reporting.

## Closed-Book Rule

- Use only the staged materials under `base/input`.
- Do not use outside web search or external regulatory knowledge.

## Inputs

- Task brief: `base/input/task_brief.md`
- Question set: `base/input/question_set.json`
- Output contract: `base/input/output_contract.json`
- Document manifest: `base/input/document_manifest.json`
- Original source files: `base/input/source_documents`
- Extracted UTF-8 text mirrors: `base/input/extracted_text`

## Your Task

Answer the three client questions in the staged brief:

1. whether leverage-related information must be reported separately through each broker for same-LEI accounts;
2. whether the staged rules provide specific numerical amounts for `流量费` and `撤单费`;
3. whether a French firm can report using only the original foreign-language software name.

## Deliverable

Write exactly one JSON file here:

- `base/output/research_answers.json`

Each top-level question key must contain:

- `conclusion`: exactly `Yes`, `No`, or `Unknown`
- `citation_document`: the Simplified Chinese source document name you rely on
- `evidence_snippet`: an exact Simplified Chinese excerpt copied from the staged source
- `answer_text`: a short English explanation
agent_must_do: Read the staged task brief, question set, output contract, document manifest, source documents, and extracted-text mirrors.
Answer all three client questions using only the staged Shanghai Stock Exchange materials.
Write exactly one JSON file to `output/research_answers.json`.
For each question, provide a `Yes`/`No`/`Unknown` conclusion, a Chinese citation, an exact Chinese evidence excerpt, and a short English explanation.
Stay closed-book and do not use outside web search or external regulatory knowledge.

input_files.name: task_brief.md
input_files.description: Agent-visible task instructions and the three client questions.

input_files.name: question_set.json
input_files.description: Structured list of the three required research questions and allowed conclusion labels.

input_files.name: output_contract.json
input_files.description: Defines the required output filename, top-level keys, and per-question JSON fields.

input_files.name: document_manifest.json
input_files.description: Maps the staged Chinese source files to their citation aliases.

input_files.name: source_documents
input_files.description: The ten original staged Shanghai Stock Exchange source files.

input_files.name: extracted_text
input_files.description: Search-friendly text mirrors of the staged Chinese source files.

rows.title: AGORA AI Governance Document Classification
rows.summary: Classify three cached AI governance documents across legislative status, technical scope, and AI lifecycle stages with verbatim evidence and a gap analysis.
rows.task_prompt:
You are working on a Linux VM as a policy analyst.

Visible task files:
- `base/input/task_spec.md`
- `base/input/taxonomy_and_instructions.md`
- `base/input/document_index.json`
- `base/input/documents/`
- `base/software/README.txt`
- `base/software/python` (optional Python helper entry point)

Your task:
1. Read `task_spec.md`, the sanitized taxonomy instructions, and all three cached document text files.
2. Classify AGORA IDs 768, 1293, and 2047 across legislative status, technical scope, and AI lifecycle stage.
3. For every TRUE label, provide a verbatim evidence quote from the corresponding cached document text.
4. Produce a cross-document matrix and a 150-300 word gap analysis.
5. Write valid JSON to:
   - `base/output/agent_output.json`

Rules:
- Do not modify files under `input/`.
- Use the cached documents under `input/documents/` as the canonical evidence source.
- Keep the final deliverable at exactly `base/output/agent_output.json`.
agent_must_do: Read input/task_spec.md, input/taxonomy_and_instructions.md, input/document_index.json, and the three cached document text files.
Classify each document across the provided legislative-status, technical-scope, and lifecycle-stage taxonomies.
Provide verbatim evidence quotes from the cached text for every TRUE label.
Write output/agent_output.json with the requested structured JSON, cross-document matrix, and gap analysis.

input_files.name: task_spec.md
input_files.description: Agent-visible task instructions and required output schema.

input_files.name: taxonomy_and_instructions.md
input_files.description: Sanitized taxonomy definitions and public task instructions.

input_files.name: document_index.json
input_files.description: Cached document titles, source URLs, and local text filenames.

input_files.name: documents
input_files.description: Cached public document text for AGORA IDs 768, 1293, and 2047.
